objections.claim: The verdict-producing dynamic closure is digest-verified but not mutation-point-bound. The plan correctly observes that hashing an open executable fd does not freeze its bytes and therefore executes the main ELF from a sealed memfd, yet it only mounts PT_INTERP, DT_NEEDED libraries, exec helpers, credential helpers, and runtime inputs in a read-only content-addressed root. A read-only bind mount does not prevent another writable alias from overwriting the same backing inode after verification and before or during loader/helper access. Consequently matching main-ELF digests can still lead to unauthenticated bytes fabricating Node/git/gh verdicts. Every closure member and verdict-affecting runtime input must be staged into an immutable snapshot whose bytes are the bytes hashed and executed/read, with an overwrite-after-verification regression covering a library, loader, helper, and trust-store input.

The claimed `pylae doctor --pin` first-run path is circular. The supported entrypoint requires the native launcher to authenticate the pinned static sandbox-builder before Node executes, and Node/git/gh/bwrap are forbidden before their operator-manifest identities and closures are pinned; however the plan assigns creation of those pins to `pylae doctor --pin`, which itself requires that launcher→builder→Node chain to execute. With no existing manifest the system must either deadlock or execute untrusted host verdict-producing bytes that can author their own trusted manifest. The approach needs an independently authenticated pre-Node provisioning mechanism, or must require an already provisioned external-tool manifest and remove the first-run TOFU claim, with a clean-room no-manifest regression proving no host tool executes.
